searchText: Replied here: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-3450-standard-for-applying-shamirs-to-bip-39-mnemonics/5844/14 > Discrete log is hard in GF(2^128) and GF(2^256). Discrete log is actually not that hard in binary fields I don't know of any polynomial time algorithm that solves this. By not that hard do you mean quasi-polynomial time? Quasi polynomial in 128 is not cryptographically secure thanks It seems even for Elliptic curve discrete log, 128 bits isn't enough either. People broke 114 bits (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrete_logarithm_records#Elliptic_curves).
